engagement_title: Cordwain Overland spring merch drop — screen-print apparel kit

garment mockup board on licensed apparel shots
printer spec sheet: plate list, ink colours, placement + max print width
square social teaser set for the store page

neutralise the photographed sample to a true white point using its in-frame reference
extract each mark clean of substrate and keep enclosed counters as holes
reduce each graphic to a defensible spot-colour count and build one plate per colour
vectorize each plate and repair viewBox/background so plates register
author the mockup board + printer spec sheet as an editable print doc
decision_gates: Which of a graphic's two inputs is the trace source — the crisp flat export or the on-garment photo — and the photo must be neutralised first or its cast seeds the wrong plate colours
How many spot colours each graphic truly needs: over-separating inflates screen cost, under-separating loses the art; the count must be justified against the print budget
Enclosed letter counters must survive as holes — a background-knockout fills them solid and only shows broken once printed on a coloured garment
element_reuse: Each graphic is vectorized ONCE; that single master feeds its separation sheet, its 1-colour reduction, the mockup board and the social teasers — any redraw between pieces is visible brand drift.
price_demo: Mid-tier outdoor apparel, tees $34 / hoodies $78, buyers 24-40 who screenshot the print detail before buying. Load-bearing: a premium outdoor buyer reads a tight 2-3 colour discharge look as quality, so a cheap-looking 6-colour plastisol separation would signal a bargain brand and misprice the whole line.
why_not_vlm: A one-shot regen redraws the graphics and cannot emit registered per-colour plates; the client needs THEIR exact marks preserved and separated into printable plates, not a lookalike raster.
doability: asset upload -> image_select_by_prompt(returnBbox) -> image_invert_selection -> image_crop_to_bounds -> image_fill_area (white knockout per colour region) / image_apply_halftone(blackAndWhite:true) for tonal fields -> image_vectorize -> local SVG hygiene (inject viewBox, strip path-0 background) -> author HTML (inline SVG plates + data:URI garment shots at mm canvas, Adobe Fonts kit) -> html_export_readiness_skill -> export_html_to_express. Garment photos come from licensed Stock at camera scale. No banned capability, no upscaling (crop_and_resize is downscale-only here), no Illustrator/vector-merge render.
options_moment: Agent proposes 2-3 separation strategies per graphic (e.g. 2-colour discharge vs 3-colour with a base plate) and justifies the pick against the stated print budget and garment colour.

key_stages: triage the printed scan vs the etched-nameplate photo and choose the correct trace source
deskew and neutralise the chosen capture using its in-frame reference
select the ink/engraving at graphic level, not the metal substrate
invert polarity correctly before tracing so the mark comes out positive
vectorize, inject viewBox, strip the background rect, and verify counters are holes
author the usage sheet + stationery mockup as an editable print doc
decision_gates: The etched-nameplate photo is a trap source — glare and bevel shadows trace into noise; the flat scan is the correct master and the photo is only a cross-check

Selection prompt wording decides everything: naming the substrate ('the mark on the plate') grabs the metal; naming the graphic's own form/colour grabs the ink — the wrong prompt yields a plate-shaped blob that still 'succeeds'
Mask polarity before vectorize — trace the raw mask and you ship a filled box with the logo knocked out of it
element_reuse: One recovered master path is the single source for every variant and the stamp/sign outline; any variant re-traced instead of derived will not overlay the master exactly.
price_demo: B2B capital-equipment maker, machines $40k-$300k, seen by procurement engineers. Load-bearing: this buyer equates precision with competence, so a wobbly auto-traced mark on a $200k machine's nameplate reads as sloppy engineering — the vector must be crisp and mechanically exact, not a soft hand-feel logo.
why_not_vlm: A model would redraw a plausible but different mark; the company's actual registered logo must be recovered and preserved to the path, delivered as editable vector, not a raster impression.
doability: image_select_by_prompt(returnBbox) -> image_invert_selection -> image_crop_to_bounds -> image_apply_adjustments (neutralise) -> image_vectorize -> SVG hygiene -> html-export usage sheet + stationery mockup. No banned capability, no upscaling, no OCR, no Illustrator render.

decision_gates: The SAME graphic needs DIFFERENT reductions per medium: embroidery can't hold fine detail (simplify + limited thread colours), enamel needs metal bridges between colours, a sticker keeps full detail — one-size art fails at least two of the three
Embroidery colour count and minimum detail are hard limits — a gradient or hairline that survives on a sticker must be redrawn as solid thread blocks for a patch
Kiss-cut offset direction and enclosed holes must be right or the sticker cut slices the art / the pin enamel wells don't close
element_reuse: One extracted graphic seeds all three medium-specific versions and the woven label — a redraw between the patch and the pin is exactly the inconsistency that breaks a coordinated pack.
price_demo: Streetwear small-goods, stickers $4 / pins $14 / patches $18. Load-bearing: the price ladder maps to fidelity — the $4 sticker keeps full detail, the $18 patch is deliberately reduced to bold thread blocks — so the same art is simplified more as the item gets more 'made', a distinction a flat regen ignores.
why_not_vlm: A model produces mockup images but not the three genuinely different manufacture-ready vector reductions of the brand's own graphics.
doability: image_remove_background (transparent) / image_select_by_prompt->invert->crop for messy exports -> image_fill_area(flatten for patch/pin plates) -> image_vectorize -> SVG hygiene (viewBox, strip path-0, offset cutline for stickers); mockups + specs via html-export. No banned capability, no upscaling, no Illustrator render.
options_moment: Agent proposes 2 embroidery reductions (3-thread vs 5-thread) and justifies one on stitch cost and legibility at patch size.

signature_op: true-colour recovery + refined wordmark/monogram vectorize for foil/engrave

Load-bearing: at this tier the mark must be hairline-refined for foil on dark stock with vast negative space, so a mass-market jewelry brand's bolder higher-contrast mark would be wrong — the delicate high-contrast refinement is exactly what the price band requires.

engagement_title: Ironway Run Club member numbering & race-bib kit

recovered club mark vector for the bib header
per-member race bibs (one print-ready page each)
a single press PDF of all bibs (page-count = roster)

engagement_title: Wren & Halloway heritage property crest recovery, signage & plaque system
